args.query: terminal windows transparent and frozen, stay open when running multiple cmd files started at same time

claude.result: {"seen_before": true, "matches": ["terminal#19269", "terminal#16612"], "answer": "This looks like a known issue. When Terminal is the default terminal application, it can open an empty, transparent window with no tabs that hangs. A script that launches several console programs at once makes this more likely. In terminal#19269, a single WindowsTerminal.exe process was hung and every Terminal window it owned froze with it. The maintainers called this the \"defterm window with no tabs\" problem. No fix has been posted in the tickets. Workarounds from the tickets: (1) End the WindowsTerminal.exe process in Task Manager. After that, new windows worked again in terminal#19269. parsed.answer: This looks like a known issue. When Terminal is the default terminal application, it can open an empty, transparent window with no tabs that hangs. A script that launches several console programs at once makes this more likely. In terminal#19269, a single WindowsTerminal.exe process was hung and every Terminal window it owned froze with it. The maintainers called this the "defterm window with no tabs" problem. No fix has been posted in the tickets. Workarounds from the tickets: (1) End the WindowsTerminal.exe process in Task Manager. After that, new windows worked again in terminal#19269. A reboot also clears it temporarily. (2) Until it is fixed, you could stagger the script's launches, for example with `start /wait` or a short `timeout`, so the three .cmd files don't start at the same instant. Alternatively, set the default terminal to 'Windows Console Host' under Settings > Privacy & security > For developers > Terminal. The tickets don't confirm either of these, so treat them as untested suggestions. To help the investigation, use Feedback Hub (Apps > Windows Terminal > Advanced Diagnostics, then record while you reproduce it). Attach that to terminal#19269. This avoids posting a memory dump publicly. Also check the Event Viewer for DCOM Event ID 10010 timeouts or a WindowsTerminal.exe crash, as reported in terminal#16612 and terminal#19269.
